data.name: Obadiah
data.gender_notes: Obadiah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Obadiah is derived from the Hebrew roots ‘obad’ (servant) and ‘yah’ (God). Its meaning can be translated as ‘Servant of YAHWEH.’ In the Old Testament, there is a book named after this prophet, Obadiah, who prophesied against the Edomites for their cruelty towards their brother Judah. The name Obadiah carries the meaning “Servant of YAHWEH” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Obadiah usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of yahweh and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes dedication and faith to God
data.etymology: Obadiah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant of YAHWEH.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Obadiah total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Obadiah
in_english.meaning: servant of the Lord, name of a prophet in the Old Testament
in_english.long_meaning: Obadiah, meaning 'servant of the Lord', is the name of a prophet in the Old Testament (1 Kings 18:3, 2 Kings 13:14 - Hebrew Bible - Old Testament). The name is derived from Hebrew roots 'servant' and 'God' or 'Lord'. In Christian tradition, Obadiah is considered a significant name due to its connection with the prophet who served under King Ahab and Elijah. The name is often associated with spiritual leadership, loyalty, and devotion to God. In modern usage, the name Obadiah is sometimes chosen for its unique and meaningful nature, reflecting the individual's desire to serve and honor the Lord.

data.cultural_impact: The name Obadiah has been borne by a number of notable figures in history. In the Bible, Obadiah is a prophet whose book is part of the Old Testament. Obadiah was also a servant of King Ahab, administering his household. There is a biblical account of Obadiah hiding 100 prophets in two hidden places to save them from being slaughtered by King Ahab. Obadiah's actions display his deep devotion and loyalty to God and His prophets. This historical background illustrates the cultural significance of the name Obadiah, representing devotion, loyalty, and courage.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Obadiah is found in its meaning - ‘Servant of YAHWEH.’ This name serves as a reminder of the primary role of every Christian, that is, to serve and obey God. Obadiah in the Bible is an embodiment of this quality, dedicated to the service of God and His prophets despite the risks involved. When we bear this name, we are called to emulate the characteristics of Obadiah, such as faithfulness, courage, and obedience to God. Let us strive to serve Him in all aspects of our lives, demonstrating our love and devotion to Him as Obadiah did.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Obadiah means "servant of the Lord" in Hebrew. This name signifies a deep commitment to serving and honoring God in all aspects of life. It is a reminder of the importance of obedience and faithfulness in the eyes of the Lord.

biblical_reference.note: name of a prophet who served under King Ahab and Elijah

historical_references.reference: Obadiah the prophet wrote a book of the Old Testament bearing his name around 850 BC during the reign of King Jehoram of Judah.
historical_references.context: During the time of the divided kingdoms of Israel and Judah, Obadiah wrote a prophecy against the Edomites for their lack of support during the Babylonian conquest of Judah.

historical_references.reference: Obadiah the biblical character is also mentioned in 1 Kings 11:2-4 as one of King Solomon's loyal ministers who warned him about the sin of marrying foreign wives, around 960-930 BC.
historical_references.context: Obadiah was a leading official under King Solomon, and he intervened to protect the faith of Israel when the king's foreign wives introduced idolatry into the kingdom.

modern_usage.modern_context: Obadiah is a minor prophet in the Jewish and Christian Bibles. His name means 'servant of Yahweh'. In modern contexts, Obadiah is often studied and discussed for his prophecies about the coming judgment of Edom. His name is seen on various platforms including Christian podcasts, religious blogs, and literary discussions, where scholars and theologians delve into the historical and symbolic significance of his writings. The general trends in these discussions revolve around understanding the biblical context and message of Obadiah, as well as its relevance to contemporary spiritual and moral issues.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Obadiah in New York, United States credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Obadiah, which means "Servant of YAHWEH". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
